history.summary: Built in 1166 CE by Rajaraja Chola II, one of the three 'Great Living Chola Temples' inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2004), with Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Designed as a stone chariot (Karakkoil) in Dravidian style, it is famed for the 'singing steps' of the Bali Pitham that emit the seven musical notes, sculpted river goddesses, and reliefs of the 63 Bhakti saints. Named after Airavata, Indra's elephant, whose white skin was restored after bathing in the temple tank. It remains an actively worshipped temple. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV lists Kumbakonam; the temple is at Darasuram (Dharasuram), ~4 km from Kumbakonam, corrected here.

name: Airavatesvara Temple
town_description: Silk-weaving town ~4 km from Kumbakonam in Thanjavur district, known almost entirely for the 12th-century UNESCO-listed Airavatesvara Chola temple and its silk weaving centres.

travel.railway: Darasuram station (local stop); Kumbakonam Railway Station, ~5 km, is the main railhead
travel.road: ~4 km from Kumbakonam; reached by auto, taxi, and state/private buses

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; early morning for photography
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM – 12:30 PM, 4:00 PM – 8:30 PM (verify: some sources give 8:00 AM – 12:00 PM / 4:00 – 7:00 PM; photography fees may apply)
